author: Shajaka Shelton
title: Lansing City Council could rename César E. Chávez Avenue - NewsBreak
text:
By Shajaka Shelton Zack Priehs ,
2 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — The legacy of César E. Chávez, the man at the front line of the fight for migrant workers’ rights is now falling apart ever since accusations of sexual abuse surfaced earlier this month. Now, the ripples are being felt right here in Mid-Michigan .
Many organizations across the country, including the farmworker’s union he helped co-found with Dolores Huerta — one of the women accusing him of sexual assault — have cancelled or renamed events formerly in his honor.
Here in Lansing, a push to rename César E. Chávez Avenue has begun — one some Lansing City Council members are openly behind.
While City Council President Peter Spadafore says the process of changing a roads name is a long one, At-Large Council Member Trini Pehlivanoglu tells 6 News the process will begin on Thursday, with a discussion at the Committee on City Operations meeting scheduled for 4 p.m.
“It seemed that this is an appropriate place to address that,” said Pehlivanoglu. “Again, the process overall does take some time, but I think it’s a good first step we’re able to talk about it.”
She says the change won’t happen overnight, and it’s one they’ll make carefully and with the entire community in mind.
“Engaging with the community overall, understanding that there was quite a movement to have the name changed to Chávez,” said Pehlivanoglu. “And really just being proactive.”
